in_arabic.name: سُهَير
in_arabic.long_meaning: هُوَ الَّذي يُقَدَّمُ لِلشَغَفِ، وَالَّذي يُغَيَّرُ لِلَّيْلِ، وَهُوَ أَخَفُّ مِنَ النِسَاءِ، وَيُقَدَّمُ لِلشَغَفِ، وَالشَغَفُ إِمامٌ لِلمَرءِ، وَهُوَ مُؤَمِّلُ الرِزقِ، وَالرِزقُ مَزِدُ النَفْسِ، وَالنَفْسُ مُضِيُّ الدُنْيَا، وَالدُنْيَا مَعاقِدُ أَمَلِ النَفسِ

in_urdu.name: سُهیر
in_urdu.meaning: رات کو بدلنے والا، خواتین سے کم
in_urdu.long_meaning: یہ وہ شخص ہوتا ہے جو رات کو بدلنے کی امید کرتا ہے، اور یہ خواتین سے کم ہوتا ہے، اور رات کا بدلنا اس کے لئے امین ہے کہ وہ روزگار کی امید کرتا ہے، روزگار انسان کی زندگی کو بڑھاتی ہے، اور زندگی دنیا کی معیشت ہے، اور دنیا کی معیشت انسان کی روح کی امید ہے

in_hindi.name: सुहैर
in_hindi.meaning: रात को बदलने वाला, स्त्रियों से कम
in_hindi.long_meaning: वह व्यक्ति जो रात को बदलने की आशा करता है, वह स्त्रियों से कम होता है, और रात को बदलना उसके लिए अमीन है कि वह दिन की उम्मीद करता है, दिन आदमी की जिंदगी को बढ़ाता है, और जीवन दुनिया की अर्थव्यवस्था है, और दुनिया की अर्थव्यवस्था आदमी की आत्मा की आशा है

in_english.name: Suhair
in_english.meaning: One who brings change to the night, softer than women
in_english.long_meaning: One who brings change to the night, softer than women, and brings hope for sustenance, sustenance is the increase of the soul, and the soul is the hope of the afterlife, and the afterlife is the reward for the good deeds of a person

data.cultural_impact: The name Suhair is derived from the Arabic word "Suhur" which means 'before sunrise'. In some Arab and Middle Eastern cultures, the word "Suhur" is also used to refer to the pre-dawn meal. Naming a child Suhair signifies that the child is a beacon of light and hope, much like the dawn.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name Suhair holds deep spiritual significance. It signifies the inner light and faith that one must carry within themselves, just as the dawn brings light to the world. Suhair symbolizes the importance of staying spiritually enlightened, even in the darkness of the night. It reminds us to inspire hope and light within ourselves and to radiate this light upon the world.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir Records Suhair bint Harith as the mother of Prophet Solomon's vizier, Asaf ibn Barkhiyyath.
historical_references.context: Old Testament and Quran mentioned Solomon's vizier Asaf, while Ibn Kathir, a renowned Islamic historian, connected this to Suhair in his work Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Tha'alibi Writes About Suhair bint Dhu'l-Kifl as a Wise Woman and a Prophetess. The name Suhair carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Tha'alibi, an Arabic historian and poet, recorded in his book Al-Amarat Al-Insaniyya stories about various wise women in Islamic history. One of those stories was about Suhair bint Dhu'l-Kifl, who was described as a prophetess and a wise woman.

modern_usage.modern_context: Suhair is a beautiful Islamic name with its origins in Arabic, meaning 'bright morning'. Traditionally, this name was given only to boys, however, in modern times, it has become increasingly popular for girls as well. The name Suhair is gaining popularity across various platforms such as social media, baby name websites and apps, and parenting and lifestyle blogs. Some of the trends contributing to its rise include the growing interest in Islamic baby names, the shift towards gender-neutral names, and the trend of reviving modern Arabic names.
